content: A sleep log is a detailed record that tracks an individual's sleep and wake patterns over a period of several weeks. It is primarily used to diagnose circadian rhythm sleep disorders and to assess the effectiveness of treatments for these disorders. A sleep log typically includes the following information: The exact time the individual attempted to fall asleep. The estimated time the individual believes they actually fell asleep. The number of nighttime awakenings, along with the specific times they occurred and their durations. The time the individual woke up in the morning. The time the individual physically got out of bed. The desired wake-up time the individual had in mind before going to sleep. Whether the individual woke up naturally, was awakened by an alarm clock, or was disturbed by external factors. Whether the individual got out of bed on their own, was prompted by an alarm clock, or was disturbed by external factors. A brief description of how the individual felt throughout the day, such as their level of alertness or fatigue. The start and end times of any naps taken during the day. A record of any medications the individual was taking, if applicable. Sleep logs are often created manually, with entries recorded on graph paper. However, specialized software designed for sleep log creation is also available for free. Alternatively, spreadsheet or database software can be used to maintain these records.
